purpose: #980 DONE criterion: the end-to-end simulation round trip. casa-rs simobserve writes a noise-free MeasurementSet; CASA 6.7.6.14's tclean and casa-rs's tclean image it with the call CASA's simanalyze makes (simutil.imtclean, dryrun); tools/casa-compat/tclean_case_matrix.py compares them.

native.revision: a363cd30a4 (main 88cace1, #1076, plus the round-trip tool and the per-case CASA isolation)

sky_model: casatestdata unittest/simobserve/core5ps.skymodel (1873 x 1873 px of 0.043 arcsec, one channel at 345 GHz); the cube scenarios use a derived 4-channel copy (10 MHz apart, channel k scaled by 1 + 0.1 k)

alma12_single.note: the unset map covers the 80-arcsec model with a 12 m mosaic (gridder mosaic, natural); the tool now maps 1 arcsec for a single pointing

alma12_mosaic.call: gridder mosaic, natural, clark, niter 500, 1920 x 1920

alma12_mosaic_briggs.call: gridder mosaic, briggs (mosweight True, per-field density), clark, niter 500

alma12_aca7_mosaic.call: vis [12 m MS, 7 m MS], gridder mosaic, briggs, clark, niter 500
alma12_aca7_mosaic.result: counts exact (500 iterations, 2 major cycles, stop 1), maxpsfsidelobe within 6e-7; psf, pb, weight and sumwt within 1e-6 nRMS; image 4.2e-3, residual 8.6e-3, model 0.10 nRMS, cyclethreshold 2e-3 relative
alma12_aca7_mosaic.verdict: justified divergence: the clean's own rounding sensitivity (aca7_sensitivity)

alma12_single_cube.verdict: refused by casa-rs: mosweight with a cube's per-channel density (#818, in progress); this scenario also ran as a mosaic (unset map)

alma12_mosaic_cube.verdict: refused by casa-rs: mosweight with a cube's per-channel density (#818, in progress)

aca7_sensitivity.question: Is the 12 m + 7 m list mosaic's difference a defect or rounding? It reproduces on the 7 m MeasurementSet alone (ACA, ten 7 m dishes, 7 fields, briggs, clark).
aca7_sensitivity.dirty_images: niter 0: the list, the list with natural weighting, the 12 m and the 7 m MeasurementSets agree within 1e-6 nRMS in every product (image, residual, psf, pb, weight, sumwt)
aca7_sensitivity.cycles: 7 m, briggs: niter 20 (one minor cycle, then the model prediction) agrees within 7e-7 with clark and with hogbom; natural weighting agrees within 9e-7 at niter 500 (3 major cycles); briggs at niter 50 agrees (model 3.4e-7), and between 50 and 100 iterations of the same first minor cycle the components diverge while the cycle's peak residual (0.0039408 / 0.0039411) and model flux (0.037867 both) still agree

perturbation.method: DATA of the 7 m MeasurementSet plus complex Gaussian noise of 1e-6 of its peak (seed 7); both implementations re-run on it
perturbation.conclusion: a 1e-6 change to the data moves CASA's own result by as much as casa-rs differs from it: this briggs clean of an extended model under a 0.31 sidelobe PSF is chaotic at the rounding level, and CASA's and casa-rs's results are equally valid (AGENTS.md: results that differ only through rounding)

matrix_driver_isolation: test_iterbot_cube_restart_updatedmask run before test_modelvis_16 in one driver process changed CASA's result for test_modelvis_16 (120 iterations against 170). With each case's CASA steps in a fresh process (tclean_case_matrix.py --casa-steps), CASA gives 170 in that order (run isolation-1).

round_trip_final.native: main 53e504e (through #1084, mosweight on a mosaic cube's per-channel density) with #1087's ALMA 12 m beam radius (lead/alma-pb-radius 8220e1c); tools at lead/sim-roundtrip 24d8125

alma12_single.call: gridder standard (one pointing), natural, clark, niter 500, 1920 x 1920
alma12_single.result: 307 iterations, 4 major cycles, stop 2, exact; every product within 5.5e-7 nRMS, masks exact. Before #1087 (the 12 m beam tabled to 3.568 degrees, not CASA's 1.784) 88 .pb mask pixels flipped at pblimit

alma12_mosaic.result: 330 iterations, 4 major cycles, stop 2, exact; worst product the residual, 3.1e-6

alma12_mosaic_briggs.result: 339 iterations, 4 major cycles, stop 2, exact; worst product the residual, 4.5e-6

alma12_aca7_mosaic.result: as round trip 1: 500 iterations, 2 major cycles, stop 1, exact; psf, pb, weight and sumwt within 7e-7; image 4.2e-3, residual 8.6e-3, model 0.10
alma12_aca7_mosaic.verdict: justified divergence: the clean's rounding sensitivity (aca7_sensitivity)

alma12_single_cube.call: gridder standard, briggs (perchanweightdensity), clark, niter 500, 4 channels, restoringbeam common
alma12_single_cube.result: 906 iterations against CASA's 907, 3 major cycles, stop 1; before any cleaning the psf differs by 3.4e-4 and sumwt by 1.2e-5, pb within 2.7e-7
alma12_single_cube.verdict: CASA bug casa-rs does not follow: the cube Briggs weightor grids its density at GridFT's rotation to the phase centre and looks it up at the MeasurementSet uvw (docs/CASA (C++) bugs.md, 'The cube Briggs weightor grids and looks up its density in different uvw frames'). The pointing is 0.0215 arcsec from simanalyze's phase centre in RA and Dec (half a model pixel), so the rotation is not the identity; see cube_frames

alma12_mosaic_cube.call: gridder mosaic, briggs (mosweight, perchanweightdensity), clark, niter 500, 4 channels
alma12_mosaic_cube.result: 1001 iterations, 3 major cycles, stop 1, exact; before any cleaning psf 3.3e-3, weight 2.2e-4, sumwt 2.4e-4, pb 1.4e-4 with 246 .pb mask pixels (pb within 5e-5 of pblimit); model 7.2e-2 after cleaning
alma12_mosaic_cube.verdict: the same CASA bug for a multi-field cube (each field's density is gridded at the image phase centre's rotation), as #1084 measured on refim_alma_mosaic.ms (#789); under natural weighting the same mosaic cube agrees (cube_frames)

cube_frames.question: Are the two cube scenarios' differences the cube density's two uvw frames, or something else?
cube_frames.pointing: casa-rs simobserve's single pointing is at RA -1.30899705244215 rad, Dec -0.401425623529829 rad, 0.0215 arcsec west and north of simanalyze's phase centre (19:00:00 -23:00:00, the model's reference direction): the model's centre pixel, half a pixel from its reference pixel. CASA 6.7.6.14's simobserve, given the same model and map, puts its pointing at the same direction to every printed digit

probes.single_cube_dirty_simanalyze_centre: niter 0 at simanalyze's phase centre: psf 3.4e-4, sumwt 1.2e-5, image 2.2e-4
probes.single_cube_dirty_field_centre: niter 0 at the pointing's own direction: psf 1.2e-7, sumwt 5.6e-8, image 8.6e-8, pb exact
probes.single_cube_field_centre: simanalyze's call (niter 500) at the pointing's own direction: 900 iterations, 3 major cycles, stop 1, all exact; psf 1.2e-7, model 1.7e-7, residual 4.6e-7, sumwt 5.6e-8, cyclethreshold and maxpsfsidelobe exact; image 2.1e-4 (the common restoring beam, below)
probes.mosaic_cube_dirty_briggs: niter 0, simanalyze's call: psf 3.3e-3, sumwt 2.4e-4, weight 2.2e-4, 246 .pb mask pixels
probes.mosaic_cube_dirty_natural: niter 0, natural weighting: every product within 1e-6; one .pb mask pixel per channel, where CASA's pb is 0.200000137 against pblimit 0.2 (CASA's single-precision mosaic weight image, as hetarray alma .3/.4, #1077)

cube_frames.common_beam: with the PSFs equal to 1.2e-7 and the four channel beams equal to every printed digit, CASA's common beam is 1.143576 x 0.978783 arcsec at 89.7815 deg and casa-rs's 1.143326 x 0.978741 at 89.8177 deg: axes within 2.2e-4 (inside the comparison's 1e-3), angle 0.036 deg (outside its 0.01). Both enclose the channel beams; they differ within one 0.1% growth step of the search ('A common beam's circular case is the reciprocal of its axis' records casa-rs searching in radians where CASA searches in arcseconds)
cube_frames.pbcor_beam: CASA writes the common beam on .image.pbcor; casa-rs wrote the per-channel restoring beams there. Fixed by lead/pbcor-common-beam (#1090): rerunning single_cube_field_centre with that branch's binary, casa-rs's .image.pbcor carries one beam, its .image's (the branch predates #1087, so its pb differs by 1.8e-4 as before that fix)
